text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Ten federal ministers and four ministers of state took oath of office on Friday, raising the strength of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's cabinet to 23, including two advisers.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has said that Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves have increased to $1.3 billion.
- The rate of infaltion for 12 months ending June 1997 has been estimated at 11.80 percent.
- The government has decided to reduce customs duty on imported crude palm oil to 7,250 rupees per tonne from 8,250 rupees.
- The government has approved a proposal from Pakistan Refinery Ltd to establish a $160 million oil terminal/jetty at Bundal island near Port Qasim.
- Six policemen were injured when a bomb exploded inside a police station in Rawalpindi on Friday.
THE NEWS

- President Farooq Leghari on Friday rejected newspaper reports accusing him and his family of assisting the United States in last month's arrest of Mir Aimal Kansi from Dera Ghazi Khan for alleged deadly shooting outside the CIA headquarters.

- President Farooq Leghari, talking to reporters after administering oath to new cabinet ministers in Islamabad on Friday, dispelled the impression that he has any differences with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and expressed his intention to go back home after his presidential term is over.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has decided to lift a ban on inter-distrcit movement of wheat.
FINANCIAL POST
- Useless, dangerous and expensive non-essential drugs have taken the Pakistan pharmaceutical market by storm, draining meagre resources of a middle class that is still in its formative phase.
THE NATION
- Seven people were killed and two dozen injured in central Punjab when first wave of heavy monsoon rains hit the country on Thursday.
- Two terrorists riding on a motorcycle shot dead an activist of a Shi'ite Moslem organisation and injured a newspaper hawker in Faisalabad town of Punjab province.
- The government decided on Friday to lift a ban on inter-district movement of the wheat flour.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif told a national population convention in Islamabad on Friday that Pakistan's ecnomic and social development was being hampered by an alarming population growth rate of 2.7 percent.
